text:
li-chen: quick heads up — the capacity dashboard for eu-west is showing admission_control reject rate climbing and some weird KPI jitter this morning

matt: saw it too, single alert at 06:12, then it dropped, then came back around 06:28. noisy alerts :confused:

infra-bot: [ALERT] eu-west-gpu-pool.admission_rejects > 100 in 5m (hosted-gpu)

ash: logs show a burst of large batched requests arriving from a small set of clients, and we also have a handful of hosts in that pool with elevated CUDA OOMs around the same window

li-chen: can someone paste the dashboard panels? I'm seeing p50/p95 token latency stable but admission_rejects and queue_time p99 spike

samira: pasting query for the reject rate panel:```promql
sum(rate(gpu_pool_admission_rejects_total{region="eu-west"}[5m])) by (pool)
```

jorge: here's a snippet from the node logs, trimmed:
```
2026-02-21T06:27:41Z pool=eu-west node=gw-12 admission_reject=27 queue_len=84 reason=capacity
2026-02-21T06:27:42Z pool=eu-west node=gw-12 cuda_oom=1 pid=2473 model=redwood-4x
2026-02-21T06:27:45Z pool=eu-west node=gw-07 admission_reject=11 queue_len=91 reason=network-timeout
```

matt: network-timeout on gw-07 + cuda_oom on gw-12 suggests two different failure modes colliding. Could be a noisy neighbor + transient egress issue to storage (KV cache)

ash: agree. I also noticed the autoscaler didn't spin up extra nodes during the spike — looks like our scale buffer was zero because we had reserved most capacity for Dedicated customers in that pool this week

li-chen: oh right — commit to dedicated reservations for Q1 reduced shared capacity headroom. That was intentional for customers but we didn't lower alert sensitivity. Ops tradeoff

samira: we should avoid alert storms. Proposal: adjust eu-west admission_reject alert to use a 10m rolling average and bump threshold to 150 for the week (temporary), while we investigate root cause

jorge: +1 for temp threshold. Also proposing we enable spillover routing to a cheaper compatible model in eu-west-d (burst fallback) — that would reduce rejects without cross-region latency

matt: cost question: spillover will use burst dedicated nodes priced differently. Do we have a quick estimate? Even small burst capacity will increase billing for the day

ash: rough calc: 4 V100-equivalent hours = ~ $40 for the spike window per region. Less than the operational noise and SLO breaches if customers see 5xxs

li-chen: action items: 1) samira adjust alert to 10m avg + threshold 150 (temp) 2) ash check autoscaler config and reserved pool allocation 3) jorge enable spillover policy in eu-west for compatible models 4) matt follow up with sales/customer ops about potential impact to dedicated customers if we re-balance headroom

samira: doing 1 now — will post updated alert rule snippet when done

ash: checking autoscaler — quick look: the scale_policy had max_unavailable set to 0 and no burst_capacity configured. Suspect the scheduler rejected new pods because of strict taints for Dedicated slices. Investigating overrides

jorge: enabling spillover in eu-west with a 5% routing rate cap to limit cost. Will monitor rejects and latency after flip. If stable we'll increase to 20%

infra-bot: [ACTION] ticket created: SRE-4521 "eu-west admission_noise + autoscale review" assigned to eng-sre oncall. Link: https://issues.internal/SRE-4521

matt: thanks. once the spillover is live, we should watch per-client request distribution — need to make sure one noisy customer isn't just shifting load around and hitting fallback too

li-chen: agreed. can we add a short-lived eval that simulates large batched requests to verify behaviour?

ash: yes. I'll spin up a repro job against a staging pool with the same autoscale+taint settings. If we reproduce, we'll add a targeted rate-limiter per-client to avoid pool-wide rejects

samira: alert updated:```yaml
alert: EuWestAdmissionRejectsHigh
expr: avg_over_time(sum(rate(gpu_pool_admission_rejects_total{region="eu-west"}[5m])) by (pool)[10m:]) > 150
for: 2m
labels:
  team: eng-sre
  temp: true
```

li-chen: perfect. i'll keep this thread updated. please post any new anomalies. thanks all :thumbsup:

jorge: initial metrics after spillover flip: admission_rejects down ~60% in the 5m window, p99 latency +30ms on routed requests (within expected). continuing to monitor

matt: nice. keep an eye on billing alerts for eu-west burst usage

li-chen: final note: follow-up postmortem only if we see recurring incidents. otherwise mark as mitigated once autoscaler fixes are deployed and reject rate stays low for 24h

infra-bot: [STATUS] SRE-4521 updated: mitigations applied, monitoring 24h

samira: marking thread resolved in slack after 24h with stable metrics
